title: Merge K Sorted Lists
description: Given an array of k sorted linked lists, merge them into one single sorted linked list and return its head. An optimal solution uses a divide and conquer approach, similar to merge sort, to repeatedly merge two lists at a time until only one list remains.

steps.note: Initial call to `mergeKLists`. The input `lists` represents an array of head node indices for our global `ALL_NODES` array. `lists` is not empty.
Calling the recursive `merge` function with the full range of lists (from index 0 to 2).
`start` (0) is not equal to `end` (2). Proceed with divide and conquer.
Calculating `mid = (0 + 2) / 2 = 1`.
Recursively calling `merge` for the left half: lists[0] and lists[1] (range `start=0`, `mid=1`).
`start` (0) is not equal to `end` (1). Proceed to divide again.
Calculating `mid = (0 + 1) / 2 = 0`.
Recursively calling `merge` for the left half: lists[0] (range `start=0`, `mid=0`).
`start` (0) is equal to `end` (0). Base case reached: a single list.
Returning `lists[0]`, which is the head node with index 0 (value 1).
Back from recursive call. `l1_head_id` is now 0. Recursively calling `merge` for the right half: lists[1] (range `mid+1=1`, `end=1`).
`start` (1) is equal to `end` (1). Base case reached.
Returning `lists[1]`, which is the head node with index 3 (value 1).
Back from recursive calls. Now merging the two sorted lists: `1->4->5` (head 0) and `1->3->4` (head 3).
In `mergeTwoLists`, `l1_head_id` (0) is not null.
`l2_head_id` (3) is not null.
Creating a dummy node (ID 8) for the merged list and adding it to `ALL_NODES`.
`curr_merged_tail` points to the dummy node (ID 8).
Both `ptr1` (0) and `ptr2` (3) are not null. Enter merge loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[0].val` (1) vs `ALL_NODES[3].val` (1). `1 < 1` is false.
Since `ptr2.val` is not less, link `curr_merged_tail` (node 8) to `ptr2` (node 3).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 3).
Advance `ptr2` to its next node (node 4).
Both `ptr1` (0) and `ptr2` (4) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[0].val` (1) vs `ALL_NODES[4].val` (3). `1 < 3` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 3) to `ptr1` (node 0).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 0).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 1).
Both `ptr1` (1) and `ptr2` (4) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[1].val` (4) vs `ALL_NODES[4].val` (3). `4 < 3` is false.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 0) to `ptr2` (node 4).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 4).
Advance `ptr2` to its next node (node 5).
Both `ptr1` (1) and `ptr2` (5) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[1].val` (4) vs `ALL_NODES[5].val` (4). `4 < 4` is false.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 4) to `ptr2` (node 5).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 5).
Advance `ptr2` to its next node (null).
`ptr2` is null. Loop terminates.
`ptr1` (1) is not null. Append the remaining elements of `ptr1` to `curr_merged_tail`.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 5) to `ptr1` (node 1).
Return `ALL_NODES[dummy_node_id].next`, which is node 3 (head of `1->1->3->4->4->5`). This is the result of merging lists[0] and lists[1].
Back from recursive call. `l1_head_id` is now 3. Recursively calling `merge` for the right half of the *original* problem: lists[2] (range `mid+1=2`, `end=2`).
`start` (2) is equal to `end` (2). Base case reached.
Returning `lists[2]`, which is the head node with index 6 (value 2).
Back from recursive calls. Now merging the two sorted lists: `1->1->3->4->4->5` (head 3) and `2->6` (head 6).
In `mergeTwoLists`, `l1_head_id` (3) is not null.
`l2_head_id` (6) is not null.
Creating a new dummy node (ID 9) for the final merged list and adding it to `ALL_NODES`.
`curr_merged_tail` points to the new dummy node (ID 9).
Both `ptr1` (3) and `ptr2` (6) are not null. Enter merge loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[3].val` (1) vs `ALL_NODES[6].val` (2). `1 < 2` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 9) to `ptr1` (node 3).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 3).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 0).
Both `ptr1` (0) and `ptr2` (6) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[0].val` (1) vs `ALL_NODES[6].val` (2). `1 < 2` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 3) to `ptr1` (node 0).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 0).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 4).
Both `ptr1` (4) and `ptr2` (6) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[4].val` (3) vs `ALL_NODES[6].val` (2). `3 < 2` is false.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 0) to `ptr2` (node 6).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 6).
Advance `ptr2` to its next node (node 7).
Both `ptr1` (4) and `ptr2` (7) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[4].val` (3) vs `ALL_NODES[7].val` (6). `3 < 6` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 6) to `ptr1` (node 4).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 4).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 5).
Both `ptr1` (5) and `ptr2` (7) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[5].val` (4) vs `ALL_NODES[7].val` (6). `4 < 6` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 4) to `ptr1` (node 5).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 5).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 1).
Both `ptr1` (1) and `ptr2` (7) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[1].val` (4) vs `ALL_NODES[7].val` (6). `4 < 6` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 5) to `ptr1` (node 1).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 1).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (node 2).
Both `ptr1` (2) and `ptr2` (7) are not null. Continue loop.
Compare values: `ALL_NODES[2].val` (5) vs `ALL_NODES[7].val` (6). `5 < 6` is true.
Link `curr_merged_tail` (node 1) to `ptr1` (node 2).
Move `curr_merged_tail` to the newly added node (node 2).
Advance `ptr1` to its next node (null).
`ptr1` is null. Loop terminates.
`ptr1` is null. Skip the first `if` condition.
`ptr2` (7) is not null. Append the remaining elements of `ptr2` to `curr_merged_tail`.
Return `ALL_NODES[dummy_node_id].next`, which is node 3 (head of `1->1->2->3->4->4->5->6`). This is the final merged list.
All merges completed. The final head node 3 (representing `1->1->2->3->4->4->5->6`) is returned by `mergeKLists`.
